title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-03-04
body:
Serving Runtime - Weekly Update (kernels, KV cache, batching)
Week: 2026-02-28 -> 2026-03-06
Author: Avery Chen
Reviewed by: Samir Patel, Maya Thompson

Summary:
- This week focused on kernel work (attention/fusion improvements), KV cache reliability and serialization, and adaptive batching rollout for latency-sensitive routes. Early canary results look promising: throughput up ~10-12% on medium-length prompts, p95 latency improved ~15% on the short prompt workload.

Kernel work
- Completed prototype of fused attention + rotary prep for 8-bit and 16-bit paths (PR #412). Initial microbenchmarks show ~18% perf gain on A100 L4 for 2048-seq synthetic test.
- Reworked matmul scheduling for small-batch paths; reduced kernel launch overhead. This landed as a behind-a-flag change (PR #419).
- Known regression: 8-bit fused kernels increase peak GPU memory ~120MB on models >7B due to temporary buffers. Tracking with RR-987. Short-term mitigation: enable streaming KV eviction earlier for large seq lengths.
- Action items:
  - Samir: follow up on cuBLAS vs custom GEMM thresholds; add automated threshold tuning test (due 2026-03-10).
  - Priya: add telemetry for buffer high-water marks to help triage memory regressions (due 2026-03-08).

KV cache
- Improvements:
  - Stable serialization format for KV cache snapshots (v1) implemented; used for fast warm-start on Dedicated nodes. Verified round-trip with test suite.
  - Eviction policy refined: LRU + size-aware eviction to prioritize prefix reuse. Reduced cache churn in canary by ~22%.
- Reliability:
  - Fixed several race conditions surfaced by heavy concurrent inference tests (see RR-1012). These caused occasional panics during concurrent writes; regression tests added.
- Performance:
  - Hot-prefix cache hit rate for our internal chat workload improved from 63% -> 79% with prefix canonicalization and normalized tokenization.
- Action items:
  - Maya: expand KV cache unit tests to cover cross-process serialization edge cases (due 2026-03-12).
  - Avery: coordinate a canary that tests serialized snapshot restore under load (start 2026-03-05).

Batching and scheduler
- Adaptive batching alpha rolled to canary routes (low-latency tier). The scheduler now adjusts target batch size by observing observed latency vs SLO.
- Results from canary (72h): average throughput +12% for completion-heavy traffic, p95 latency reduced from 220ms -> 185ms on 1-2 token responses. Tail spikes still present for >8 token responses when combined with large KV restores.
- Changes made:
  - Introduced backpressure signal from network layer to scheduler when queue depth > threshold.
  - Improved batching window heuristics to aggressively flush when nearing SLO and when tokens per-request predict small outputs.
- Blockers:
  - A race between batching flush and KV restore can cause duplicate work on rare paths — tracked as RR-1012.
- Action items:
  - Liam: add metrics for batch composition by model + route to help tune heuristics (due 2026-03-09).
  - Eng-sre: validate the new backpressure thresholds in staging under synthetic spike (scheduled 2026-03-06).

Standup notes / daily highlights
- Mon 2026-03-02: Kernel PR #412 landed in feature branch; discovered memory bump on large models. Began work on telemetry.
- Tue 2026-03-03: KV cache serialization merged; ran restore tests across Dedicated nodes.
- Wed 2026-03-04: Adaptive batching canary started for low-latency routes. Observed initial throughput gains.
- Thu 2026-03-05: Follow-ups for memory regression and race fixes.
- Fri 2026-03-06: Weekly sync planned to decide canary expansion.

Metrics snapshot (canary):
- Throughput: +12% relative vs baseline (mixed route workload).
- p95 latency (short responses): 220ms -> 185ms.
- KV cache hit rate (chat workload): 63% -> 79%.
- GPU utilization: modest increase (~6%), within acceptable bounds for Dedicated canary.

Risks and blockers
- Memory regression on 8-bit fused kernels (RR-987) — blocks broad rollout to large models.
- Race in batching vs KV restore causing duplicate work and occasional increased latency (RR-1012).
- Flaky e2e tests around multi-shard restores; intermittent failure under heavy concurrency.

Decisions needed
- Approve temporary enablement of streaming eviction for large-model routes to mitigate memory bump for next two weeks? (pro: prevents OOMs on canary; con: may increase cold-start latency).
- Prioritize race fix (RR-1012) over additional kernel tuning deploys for this cycle? Team leaning: fix race first.

Next week plan
- Stabilize kernel memory behavior: add buffer pooling and reduce temporary allocations. (Owner: Samir)
- Complete KV cache cross-process tests and run larger Dedicated restore canary. (Owner: Maya + Avery)
- Tune adaptive batching heuristics based on canary metrics; deploy new batch composition metrics. (Owner: Liam)
- Remove feature-flag gating for matmul scheduling if memory regression resolved.

Notes / links
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412, https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/419
- JIRA: RR-987 (kernel memory regression), RR-1012 (batching/KV race)
- Confluence draft: (internal) confluence.redwood/serving-runtime/kernel-kv-batching-draft (TODO: link)

Meeting attendees (weekly sync): Avery Chen (owner), Samir Patel, Maya Thompson, Liam O'Connor, Priya Nair, Devon Park (observability), Erin Walsh (eng-sre)

Action item recap (short)
- Samir: automated GEMM threshold test + memory optimizations (due 2026-03-10)
- Priya: telemetry for buffer high-water marks (due 2026-03-08)
- Maya: KV serialization edge-case tests (due 2026-03-12)
- Liam: batch composition metrics and dashboard (due 2026-03-09)
- Avery: coordinate canary for serialized restore (start 2026-03-05)

Status: in_review — seeking feedback from observability and eng-sre on canary thresholds and memory mitigation approach.
